findings.rationale: WA (largest client, n=11181) uploads updates with norm far above the federation median in every round: median norm_ratio 2.198 (noise-adjusted z=+4.4), with per-round norm ratios of 2.2-2.7 in rounds 1-8 and still 1.3-1.7 in rounds 16-20. In early rounds its update is almost perfectly aligned with the coordinate-wise median (cos 0.91-0.98), which is the signature of a scaled (boosted) honest-direction update rather than random noise. Feature drift for WA is negligible (max shift 0.055 SD), so the anomaly is in the uploaded update, not the data. Cosine later decays toward 0.24, which is consistent with a manipulated upload that no longer tracks the honest consensus. Confidence is moderate: the scale is clear, but the classification of poisoning versus noise-type instability rests on the early-round alignment. Note that the broad screen's VI, DE and GU feature/subgroup outliers did not survive narrow re-queries and were not reported.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with the all-client views of client_updates, client_performance, drift_by_round, feature_summary and subgroup_outcomes (Sex, AgeGroup, Income), then confirmed leads with narrow queries. One client is reported: WA, poisoning (scaled updates, norm about 2x the median in every round, early-round cosine about 0.98 with the consensus), onset round 1, moderate confidence (0.6). Leads not reported: GU (client-wide observed rate above predicted, O/E 1.39-1.68 by sex, prevalence 0.204 vs predicted 0.134, but marginal at about z=3 and only from one client's labels, so it could be label noise or prevalence shift); CT AgeGroup 12 (observed 0.905 vs predicted 0.007, but the direction is opposite to subgroup under-diagnosis and it could not be confirmed with the remaining budget). The large VI, DE, DC and WV feature outliers in the broad screen did not hold up under narrow re-queries (VI Stroke mean 0.69 -> 0.065; VI PhysHlth -24 -> 2.2; DE GenHlth p01 -0.93 -> 0.57, no sentinel), so they were treated as noise. Budget fully spent (20.0).
